q_practical: My granddaughter's son became a high-ranking religious official - does that stop me from eating the sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why would having a distinguished descendant through your daughter's line actually block you rather than help you?

q_practical: If my grandson had a child with an enslaved woman, does that child affect who in the family can eat the sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why do children born to an enslaved parent not count at all when tracing family lineage?

q_practical: I was married to a priest, had a son, he died, and I remarried an ordinary man - can I still eat the priestly food?
q_conceptual: Why does a woman's eating rights depend on which of her sons from different husbands is still alive?

q_practical: My mother married an outsider, then remarried a priest, and that second husband died - can she still eat the sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why can a son from one marriage keep his mother eligible even after her later husband dies?

q_practical: My daughter's husband just died and they had no children - can she move back home and eat from my table again?
q_conceptual: Why does having no surviving children let a widow return to her birth family's eating privileges?

q_practical: If a widow returns to her father's house, can she eat every part of a sacrifice or just some of it?
q_conceptual: Why would a phrase granting her 'bread' be read narrowly to exclude certain other foods?

q_practical: Is a baby born without a foreskin allowed to eat sacred food without being circumcised?
q_conceptual: Why does uncertain physical sex status block someone from eating the sacred food until it's resolved?

q_practical: If a priest suffers an injury to his genitals, can his wife still eat the sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why would a husband's physical condition affect his wife's eating rights rather than just his own?

q_practical: Does it matter whether a man was born infertile or became that way later, for his household's eating rights?
q_conceptual: Why does the cause of a man's infertility change what his household is allowed to eat?

q_practical: If my household servant buys a servant of their own, can that new person eat our family's sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why does an acquisition made by someone who was themselves acquired still count toward eating rights?

q_practical: My daughter comes from a priestly family but married an outsider - can her household servants eat the sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why would marrying outside the priestly family cut off a household's servants from the food, even though they did nothing themselves?

q_practical: My wife brought servants into our marriage that legally stay hers, not mine - can they eat our sacred food even though our marriage isn't fully valid?
q_conceptual: Why does it matter whether servants are legally the wife's separate property or transferred to the husband?

q_practical: If a widow gets engaged to someone she isn't actually allowed to marry, can she still eat the sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why does simply being promised to someone in a forbidden match block a woman's eating rights, even before any wedding happens?

q_practical: My husband died and I have several brothers-in-law, one of whom isn't allowed to marry me - does that block me from eating the sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why does being tied to just one ineligible potential husband cancel a woman's rights, even though she has other eligible options too?

q_practical: My late husband's brother divorced me after the family ceremony - can I still eat the sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why would a divorce that's only forbidden by a later added rule, not by the original law, leave a woman's rights intact?

q_practical: If a priest is ritually clean himself but eats food that became impure, does he get punished for it?
q_conceptual: Why does a rule framed as a positive instruction carry a lighter penalty than an outright prohibition?

q_practical: If a man loses his hearing and speech after marrying, does his wife still get to eat the sacred food?
q_conceptual: Why does the timing of when someone loses the ability to hear or speak change a couple's eating rights?

q_practical: If a man assaults a woman and she has his child, does that child affect her eating status the normal way?
q_conceptual: Why do certain kinds of relationships not count toward establishing family lineage at all?

q_practical: A woman was assaulted by a priest and had a child from it - can she eat the sacred food because of that child?
q_conceptual: Why do we assume a child belongs to a particular man even when there's real uncertainty about who the father is?

q_practical: My husband just died - do I have to wait to find out if I'm pregnant before I'm allowed to eat the sacred food again?
q_conceptual: Why is an early pregnancy not treated as fully real until 40 days have passed?

q_practical: My husband died while I was pregnant - do our servants get to keep eating the sacred food because of the unborn child?
q_conceptual: Why does a child have to actually be born before it can affect anyone else's rights?

q_practical: If my daughter marries a man who can't hear or speak, can she eat the sacred food, and does it matter which of them is the priest?
q_conceptual: Why would a marriage to someone who can't hear or speak count as valid in one direction but not the other?

q_practical: My husband's other wife says he died - do I have to stop eating the sacred food based just on her say-so?
q_conceptual: Why isn't certain people's testimony enough on its own to change someone's legal status?

q_practical: I'm fattening a priest's cow for a cut of the profit - am I allowed to feed it the sacred grain?
q_conceptual: Why does legal ownership of an animal's body, rather than who profits from it, decide what it can be fed?

q_practical: Can I feed sacred grain to a calf that's already destined to be given to the priest?
q_conceptual: Why would an animal already owed to the priest be treated differently from other livestock?

q_practical: What amenities should I check a town has before deciding to settle there long-term?
q_conceptual: Why would access to a doctor, a court, and a public bath be treated as essential infrastructure rather than luxuries?

q_practical: Does a child born from an affair still get an equal share of their father's inheritance?
q_conceptual: Why does the legitimacy of how a child was conceived not affect inheritance, while the mother's legal status does?

q_practical: I had children before I converted, and now I have a son with my current wife - does the new son count as my firstborn for inheritance?
q_conceptual: Why can a legal 'firstborn' status reset depending on who counts as a recognized child?

q_practical: My mother remarried quickly after my father died, so I might be either man's son - do I inherit from either of them?
q_conceptual: Why does genuine uncertainty about a child's father result in that child inheriting from neither side?

q_practical: My mother remarried my father's brother quickly after my father died, and I might be either man's son - who do I inherit from?
q_conceptual: Why does a paternity doubt end up splitting an inheritance claim between two men rather than requiring proof either way?

q_practical: My cousins and I are dividing our grandfather's estate, but there's doubt about whether I'm really their brother or their cousin - how much do I get?
q_conceptual: Why is an heir whose status is uncertain given the smaller of the two possible shares rather than an even split?

q_practical: Everyone says my uncle died overseas, but there's no solid proof - can the family start dividing his property yet?
q_conceptual: Why is the bar for proving someone's death set higher for splitting an estate than for letting a widow remarry?

q_practical: My sister-in-law says her husband died overseas - can she remarry on just her word, and does that also release the estate to his heirs?
q_conceptual: Why does a widow's own statement work to free her for remarriage but not to release her husband's property to his heirs?

q_practical: If someone forces a non-Jew at gunpoint to worship an idol, are they held responsible for doing it?
q_conceptual: Why are non-Jews given more leeway under coercion than Jews are for the same act?

q_practical: If someone converts after committing a serious crime, are they punished for what they did beforehand?
q_conceptual: Why would converting erase liability for some past wrongs but not others?

q_practical: What determines which method is used when someone is sentenced to death for this kind of offense?
q_conceptual: Why would the same category of crime carry different execution methods depending on the victim's marital status?

q_practical: Is it actually forbidden to graft two different kinds of fruit trees together?
q_conceptual: Why would something be officially forbidden and even carry a theoretical death penalty, yet never actually be enforced that way?

q_practical: Are all of Abraham's descendants required to be circumcised, or only some of them?
q_conceptual: Why wouldn't a commandment given to one ancestor automatically pass down to every one of his descendants?

q_practical: Since two related ancestral groups became mixed together over time, are all their descendants expected to circumcise on the eighth day?
q_conceptual: Why would a group become obligated in a ritual through ancestral mixing rather than through a direct command to them?

q_practical: Can someone outside the faith invent their own new religious holiday or day of rest?
q_conceptual: Why is inventing a new religious practice treated as a serious violation rather than a harmless personal choice?

q_practical: What were the very first national tasks a people were expected to carry out after settling their own land?
q_conceptual: Why would setting up a government, fighting a specific enemy, and building a central shrine all be grouped together as one set of obligations?

q_practical: Can a former ruler's widow remarry, even to another ruler?
q_conceptual: Why would someone connected to a former ruler be permanently barred from remarrying, unlike an ordinary widow?

q_practical: Why would a head of state be required to keep a personal copy of a sacred text with him at all times, even in court and at meals?
q_conceptual: Why is a ruler held to a stricter personal standard than an ordinary citizen for the same underlying obligation?

q_practical: Is there a cap on how many spouses a ruler is allowed to have?
q_conceptual: Why would a leader face a numeric limit on marriages that ordinary people don't face?

q_practical: Can a head of state keep extra horses purely for show, like a ceremonial escort?
q_conceptual: Why would accumulating even one extra horse for prestige be treated as a punishable overreach?

q_practical: Is a ruler allowed to build up a large personal fortune while in office?
q_conceptual: Why draw a line between wealth held for the state's needs and wealth held for personal pride?

q_practical: If my boss gives me a direct order that conflicts with a religious duty I feel obligated to do, whose instruction wins?
q_conceptual: Why would even a minor religious duty take precedence over a direct order from someone in authority?

q_practical: Does a government have the legal right to charge taxes and tariffs on trade?
q_conceptual: Why is a ruler's right to tax treated as an inherent entitlement rather than something the people grant?

q_practical: Is there a legal difference between a formally married wife and a less formal partner for someone in a position of high status?
q_conceptual: Why would a relationship formed with less formality still count as legitimate for someone in that position?

q_practical: How is loot from a military campaign supposed to be split between the soldiers who fought and those who guarded the camp?
q_conceptual: Why would people who stayed behind guarding supplies get an equal share of the spoils as those who actually fought?

q_practical: Does a leader need government approval before going to war, or can they just decide on their own?
q_conceptual: Why would a defensive or obligatory war require no permission while an optional war requires checks and balances?

q_practical: What is a soldier supposed to do if he wants to bring home a woman he took captive during a war?
q_conceptual: Why would someone be required to wait a month and let a captive visibly grieve before making the relationship permanent?

q_practical: What basic rules is every human being, not just one particular group, expected to follow?
q_conceptual: Why would some moral rules be seen as binding on everyone through reason alone, yet still need to be formally commanded?

q_practical: What counts as a valid court system for a society not bound by the full body of religious law?
q_conceptual: Why would a lower standard of evidence - one witness, no prior warning - apply to this group's courts?

q_practical: If someone kills an unborn child, or lets a person starve instead of using a weapon, are they guilty of murder?
q_conceptual: Why would indirect methods of causing death - starvation, exposure to danger - count the same as killing someone directly?

q_practical: Is someone still considered your parent's spouse for these purposes even if they were never legally married?
q_conceptual: Why would a biological relationship alone, without a legal marriage, still create liability for forbidden relations?

q_practical: Does being engaged, without the marriage ever being consummated, count as 'married' for the purposes of an adultery charge?
q_conceptual: Why would the legal threshold for adultery differ depending on which community the victim belongs to?

q_practical: How does an informal relationship between two servants come to be recognized as a marriage, and how is it ended?
q_conceptual: Why wouldn't a marriage among this group require any written document to begin or end it?

q_conceptual: Why don't children born to an outside or enslaved mother count as 'real' children for this purpose?

id: Mishneh Torah, Levirate Marriage and Release 1:7

q_conceptual: Why is family relationship for these specific laws traced only through the father, not the mother?

id: Mishneh Torah, Levirate Marriage and Release 1:8

q_conceptual: Why would a major change in personal status erase a legal family relationship that existed before, even between twins?

id: Mishneh Torah, Levirate Marriage and Release 2:13

q_conceptual: Why does the obligation to perform the ceremony override personal preference when only one candidate is willing?

q_conceptual: Why does whose word gets trusted in this kind of dispute change depending on how much time has passed?

q_conceptual: Why is a request for delay rejected even when there's a good reason behind it?

id: Mishneh Torah, Levirate Marriage and Release 3:13

q_conceptual: Why does the order in which two family members are reported to have died change how much a woman's account is trusted?
